title: Silence, disclosure, and half-truths
summary: Disclosure rules determine when a party must reveal information rather than remain silent. A party that chooses to speak may need to supply enough information to keep its statements from becoming misleading.
notes:
Swinton declined to impose liability for undisclosed termite damage under the rule and allegations before that court. Kannavos involved an advertised multi-family use that was unlawful: the seller’s partial description created an impression that required correction. The distinction turns on the communication and circumstances, not merely whether one party possessed information the other lacked.

Questions about active concealment, special relationships, reasonable investigation, and known mistakes may require additional doctrines. The assigned cases and notes present competing policy reasons for protecting information-gathering and for preventing deception. They do not support a single rule that buyers must discover everything or that sellers must disclose everything.

topics.disclosure: A misleading partial statement differs from silence alone.
